newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF panel calls FTC holding firm plan strict.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF panel calls FTC holding firm plan strict.

text.p: An influential advisory panel to the finance minister has told Japan"s anti-monopoly watchdog that its guidelines for lifting a decades-old ban on holding firms are too restrictive, a key panel member said on Monday.
"(Many) said it was not desirable for the guidelines to be applied as strictly as they are," Keimei Kaizuka, who heads one of the panel"s committees, told reporters.
A holding company controls one or more companies, often by having a majority of shares in them, but does not engage in a specific business.

A bill to lift a 50-year-old ban on holding companies is expected to be submitted to Japan"s current session of parliament by March 11, a Fair Trade Commission (FTC) official was quoted by a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official as saying.

The FTC explained its guidelines to the Finance Ministry"s advisory panel because the financial regulation of holding companies is a major topic of discussion in the revision of the Anti-monopoly Law, the MOF official said.
Under the draft legislation recently worked out by the FTC, three types of holding companies will continue to be banned to avoid an excessive concentration of business strength.

The three types barred from forming holding companies include extremely large corporate groups, corporate groups headed by one large financial institution and groups formed by leading companies in the same or related industries.

Under the draft, firms with assets of less than 500 billion yen will not be required to obtain prior approval from the FTC, and those with assets exceeding 500 billion yen will only have to submit their group financial statements.

In the guidelines, the FTC defined "an extremely large corporate group" as one whose combined assets exceed 20 trillion yen, keeping in mind Japan"s six major corporate groups, or so-called "keiretsu", the MOF official said.

There are six major Japanese keiretsu groups -- corporate groupings linked by cross-shareholdings and long-term business ties -- Mitsui (including Sakura Bank), Mitsubishi, Sumitomo, Fuyo (led by Fuji Bank), Sanwa Bank and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank.
Economists said the combined assets of 20 trillion yen referred to by the FTC is roughly the size of the Sumitomo Group, the smallest of the six keiretsu groups.

They said nation-wide commercial banks were examples of large financial institutions, and leading companies of an industry would be defined as those holding at least 10 pct of the market in their sector or ranking third or higher among their rivals.
